caseStudies.title: Mapping the global patent landscape of phage therapy
caseStudies.problem: Phage therapy is a fast-growing alternative to antibiotics, but nobody had mapped who patents it, where, and on what.
caseStudies.approach: Collected 5,753 patents filed 1955–2023, merged them into 2,365 patent families, identified 10 technology themes with topic modelling, and computed applicant and inventor impact in Python.
caseStudies.result: Published in Nature Biotechnology (December 2024), with all code public.

caseStudies.title: A harmonised global dataset of preprints, 1990–2025
caseStudies.problem: Preprint metadata are split across Crossref, DataCite and OpenAlex, with inconsistent server names and duplicate records.
caseStudies.approach: Built harvesters for each source, wrote rules to label preprint servers, removed duplicates and mapped every record to one server list.
caseStudies.result: About 7.9 million harmonised preprint records; dataset paper in preparation for Quantitative Science Studies.

caseStudies.title: Two decades of open access in African research
caseStudies.problem: Open-access policy for African research is debated with little continent-wide evidence.
caseStudies.approach: Analysed 854,785 articles published 2002–2021 by open-access route, collaboration pattern and funding, using OpenAlex and Unpaywall.
caseStudies.result: Manuscript in preparation. Open articles tended to be more cited, and international collaboration drove access.

caseStudies.title: Research-intelligence dashboards for clients
caseStudies.problem: Recruiters and research managers need publication and patent evidence without running their own analyses.
caseStudies.approach: Built web apps that pull OpenAlex, Crossref and Altmetric metadata on demand, a patent-trend dashboard for immune-checkpoint therapy from Lens.org data, and a research-funding dashboard on PostgreSQL.
caseStudies.result: Three working apps, plus a public Substack explaining patent and publication data.

caseStudies.title: COVID-19 research in Africa: output, collaboration and leadership
caseStudies.organisation: Kong group and co-authors in Cameroon, Canada, Italy, Rwanda and Tanzania
caseStudies.problem: It was unclear how much COVID-19 research African scientists led, and with whom they worked.
caseStudies.approach: Searched Web of Science, PubMed and African Journals Online, screened and de-duplicated records, and measured authorship and collaboration.
caseStudies.result: Published in IJERPH (2021), with the full dataset shared openly.

caseStudies.title: Exploring the human respiratory microbiota
caseStudies.problem: Most bacteria living in the human respiratory tract had never been grown or described.
caseStudies.approach: Combined culturomics with metagenomics on clinical samples, and wrote a systematic review of every bacterial species reported from the mouth and airways.
caseStudies.result: About 20 new bacterial species described; PhD defended in November 2018.
